Dans le cadre de la finale mondiale du H: As part of the global finals of the Huawei ICT Competition 2025-2026, an Algerian student delegation enjoyed an unprecedented technological immersion in China. Between visits to centers of excellence and the discovery of smart cities, this experience highlighted the challenges of digital transformation, a booming sector in Algeria where operators like Mobilis, Djezzy, and Ooredoo are doubling their efforts to modernize infrastructure.
Une expérience formatrice au cœur de l’i: A formative experience at the heart of global innovation
Alors que la compétition internationale: As the international competition organized by Huawei prepares to name its winners, an Algerian student delegation had the unique opportunity to visit the Longhua International Cooperation Center (LICC) and Xicun village, two major hubs for technological research and development in China. These visits, organized on the sidelines of the event, allowed participants to dive into smart city solutions, 5G/6G technologies, and digital transformation initiatives that are redefining global standards.
Pour l’Algérie, où le secteur des téléco: For Algeria, where the telecom sector is undergoing major changes, this immersion is of particular importance. The country is banking on modern infrastructure to reduce the digital divide and support its ambition of becoming a technological hub in Africa. National operators, Mobilis (Algérie Télécom), Djezzy (Orascom Telecom Algérie), and Ooredoo Algérie, are investing massively in 5G, IoT, and data centers, fields where Chinese innovations could inspire future partnerships.

Telecom operators play a key role in this momentum:
Mobilis (Algérie Télécom) : Leader histo: Mobilis (Algérie Télécom): As the historical leader, the public operator is accelerating the rollout of 5G and fiber-optic networks, while developing cloud solutions for businesses.
Djezzy (Orascom Telecom Algérie) : Spéci: Djezzy (Orascom Telecom Algérie): Specializing in mobile services, Djezzy is focusing on innovation with offerings like fixed 5G and partnerships for smart cities.

Ces initiatives s’inscrivent dans un con: These initiatives are part of a context where Algeria is seeking to reduce its dependence on technological imports and foster the emergence of local startups in telecom and IoT. Exchanges with Chinese players like Huawei could thus open up prospects for collaboration, particularly in the fields of smart agriculture, smart grids, and cybersecurity.
